title: smart-routing-fallback-debug-notes-taylor
content:
Summary / context:
- Notes from debugging the smart-routing + fallback/regional failover behavior during the 2025-02-14 incident where traffic from EU region saw 503s and long tails, and some requests were not falling back as expected to alternative capacity tiers.
- Affected customers: subset of Hosted API customers behind route: customer-alpha-prod (customer id cid-0a1b).
- Symptom window: ~2025-02-14 17:23 -> 17:50 UTC. Intermittent 502/503 + 5xx from gateway and some upstream "no healthy upstream" logs from router.

Raw breadcrumbs / logs (sanitized):
- 2025-02-14T17:24:03Z [router] level=error msg="dispatch failed" request_id=req-4f2a path=/v1/completions status=503 upstream_error="no healthy upstream" route=customer-alpha-prod region=eu-west1
- 2025-02-14T17:24:04Z [fallback-manager] level=info msg="fallback decision" request_id=req-4f2a chosen_variant=model-7quant fallback_attempted=true reason="overloaded"
- 2025-02-14T17:24:04Z [router] level=warn msg="fallback failed: target unavailable" request_id=req-4f2a target=dedicated-us-east1 status=503
- 2025-02-14T17:25:10Z [autoscaler] level=info msg="scale event" pool=dedicated-eu-west1 delta=+2 current=10 reason="cpu>80%"
- 2025-02-14T17:26:12Z [cache] level=error msg="redis.ClusterDownError" err="CLUSTERDOWN Local alives 0"

Commands / checks I ran (order approximate):
1) Replayed customer request through staging router to replicate:
   curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" -H "X-Region: eu-west1" \
     -d '{"model":"model-7","input":"test"}' https://staging-api.internal.redwood/v1/completions
   -> got 503, router log matched request_id above.

2) Checked routing table for customer-alpha-prod via admin API:
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer admin-token" \
     https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/routes/customer-alpha-prod | jq
   Observed: primary_region: eu-west1, fallback_policy: AUTO, fallback_targets: [dedicated-us-east1, hosted-variant], max_latency_ms: 500

3) Queried fallback-manager state for that route:
   GET https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/fallbacks/customer-alpha-prod
   Returned: last_evaluated: 2025-02-14T17:23:58Z, last_action: ATTEMPTED_REROUTE, action_status: TARGET_UNAVAILABLE, notes: "dedicated-us-east1 unreachable (dial tcp timeout)"

4) Verified network connectivity from router pod in eu-west1 to dedicated-us-east1 endpoints:
   kubectl exec -n router -it router-pod-5 -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -sS -w "%{http_code}
" -o /dev/null http://dedicated-us-east1.cluster.internal/health'
   -> timed out (no response).
   kubectl exec ... -- traceroute dedicated-us-east1.cluster.internal -> shows last hop failing across inter-region peering.

5) Inspect Redis (prefix cache + routing-state store):
   redis-cli -h redis-eu.z internal
   > GET route:customer-alpha-prod:state
   -> returns JSON blob (sanitized) including last_reroute_ts and candidate_list. Also saw error when running: (error) CLUSTERDOWN

6) Autoscaler & capacity checks:
   - Query metrics for dedicated-eu-west1 pool: 95th p95 token-latency increased, CPU at 92% at 17:23.
   - dedicated-us-east1 shows healthy metrics from control plane, but router pod couldn't reach it (network).

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1 (most likely): Inter-region network issue (peering / firewall change) prevented fallback to dedicated-us-east1; fallback-manager tried, but target was unreachable, resulting in 503s. Supporting evidence: traceroute timeouts, curl timeouts, redis CLUSTERDOWN around same time (could indicate control plane/redis partitioning).
- H2: Redis cluster/coordination problem caused fallback-manager to think targets were unavailable or to drop fallback actions. Logs show redis errors; if redis cluster lost majority, fallback decision writes may have failed.
- H3: A recent routing config rollout removed hosted-variant from fallback targets for this customer by mistake (PR #1234 touched fallback target list for customer segments). Less likely because admin API shows hosted-variant still present.
- H4: Autoscaler thrash: rapid scale-down in eu pool during spike caused transient lack of capacity and inconsistent health reports; fallback didn't kick to hosted due to strict max_latency_ms and host-tier constraints.

Quick repro attempts / notes: 
- Replaying from router in eu-west1 ALWAYS reproduces the 503 when trying to reach dedicated-us-east1, but curl directly to hosted-variant returns 200.
- Manual admin API reroute to hosted-variant works:
   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer admin" 
     https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/routes/customer-alpha-prod/reroute -d '{"target":"hosted-variant"}'
   -> subsequent requests served successfully.

Immediate mitigations applied (during incident):
- Emergency policy: set fallback_policy=FORCE_HOSTED for customer-alpha-prod at 17:29 UTC (admin change) -> traffic recovered.
- Pagerduty: paged networking team to investigate cross-region peering.
- Opened ticket INF-4321 to track root cause and postmortem.

Outstanding questions / follow-ups:
- Why did redis report CLUSTERDOWN at the exact time? Was there a maintenance / OS kernel upgrade on redis nodes in eu region? Check infra-sre changelog.
- Was there a config push (CI) around 17:20 that touched firewall/peering rules? Check PRs and infra change log.
- Does fallback-manager have sufficient circuit-breaker thresholds? Currently it marks target unavailable after 2 consecutive dial timeouts of 3s each. Consider changing to attempt hosted fallback sooner for critical routes.
- Are health-check endpoints exposed across inter-region peering, or do we rely on control plane health signals only? The router attempted direct curl health check and timed out.

Next steps (owners assigned inline):
- [infra-net] (Marcus) Investigate inter-region peering between eu-west1 and us-east1 (traceroutes, BGP logs, firewall rules). Check any changes 17:00-17:30 UTC.
- [infra-db] (Olivia) Investigate redis cluster CLUSTERDOWN: node logs, failover events, maintenance windows. (INF-4321)
- [eng-sre] (me/Taylor) Add extra logging around fallback-manager decisions (dump candidate list + last 3 health checks) and increase fallback to hosted trial for critical customers for next 24h.
- [product] Review customer-alpha-prod fallback constraints (max_latency_ms, excluded_targets) to ensure hosted fallback allowed for critical customers.

Notes for postmortem draft:
- Timeline with decision points and state transitions (router->fallback_manager->target selection).
- Evidence that network partition (or redis partition) was root contributor.
- Proposed mitigations: reduce timeouts for fallback to hosted, add cross-region health-check monitoring, improve redis HA topology across regions, and an automated circuit-breaker override to pick hosted fallback if inter-region unreachable.

Scratch ideas (not decided):
- Pre-warming a hosted-variant warm pool per customer segment to allow faster fallback with lower tail-latency impact.
- Add "regional-failover whitelist" where if cross-region peering is suspected (BGP anomalies), system automatically sets FORCE_HOSTED for pre-approved customers until peering restored.

Appendix: useful commands / snippets used during debug:
- Get router logs around timestamp:
  kubectl -n router logs router-pod-5 --since=40m | grep req-4f2a -n
- Query fallback-manager state (direct):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer admin" https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/debug/fallbacks?route=customer-alpha-prod | jq
- Redis quick check:
  redis-cli -h redis-eu-01.cluster.internal -p 6379 --raw ping
- Force reroute to hosted (admin):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer admin" \
    https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/routes/customer-alpha-prod/override -d '{"fallback_policy":"FORCE_HOSTED","reason":"incident-2025-02-14"}'

Open/unknowns to capture in postmortem:
- exact series of infra changes (if any) that correlate to CLUSTERDOWN / peering issue; coordinate with infra change log and cloud provider support.
- whether any other customers experienced similar fallback failures but were masked by different route configs.

End notes / personal todo:
- Draft postmortem skeleton and share with Olivia + Marcus by EOD 2025-02-19.
- Add a short runbook entry for emergency FORCE_HOSTED switch and hookup to incident playbook.

Tags (for search): incident, fallback, smart-routing, regional, network, redis, debug
